To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Campanulales are a well-supported clade, and that within this clade, the Campanulidae are a well-supported group that includes the families Campanulaceae and Cyphiaceae, whereas the Lobeliidae are a well supported group that includes the family Lobeliaceae.
the chloroplast genomes of eighteen representatives of the Campanulales are highly rearranged and the gene order changes support a reasonably well resolved family phylogeny.

the chloroplast genomes of the Campanulacea show many more rearrangements than other plants, that these rearrangements are highly informative, and that the resulting phylogenies provide a better understanding of relationships among the taxa.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evolution and utility of chloroplast genomes in phylogenetic inference and the results are of general importance in understanding the evolution of plant genomes and in the systematics of angiosperms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

gene order data, when combined with other sources of information (i.e., ITS and rbc L sequence data), provide a powerful tool for phylogenetic analysis of plant taxa and that the chloroplast genome is an excellent source of phylogenetic characters for this type of work.
the gene order data are a useful addition to other molecular data sets for phylogenetic studies of Campanulid species.
the phylogeny of Campanulid genera and species is best resolved using a combination of cpDNA gene order, ITS, and rbcL sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene order data are useful for phylogenetic analysis of plant taxa with highly rearranged cpDNA.
gene order changes are a valuable tool for phylogenetics.
chloroplast genome rearrangements are useful in resolving phylogenetic relationships in the Campanula family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene order data can be a powerful tool in plant phylogenetics.
the use of cpDNA rearrangments can be a very useful tool for phylogenetic inference.
the chloroplast genome is a useful tool for phylogenetics, even in a group where rearrangements are common.
